content: 1. Asenapine increases the QTc interval, which can enhance its toxicity. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely when using asenapine. 2. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that carry a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, as both rilpivirine and asenapine transdermal formulations can prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can reduce rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 4. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. If antacids are necessary, they should be administered at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours afterward. 5. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 6. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 7. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 8. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. 9. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 10. Calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate all decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 11. Calcium/vitamin D combinations decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 12. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of chlorpromazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 13. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 15. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of citalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 16. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 17. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 18. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of clomipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 19. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 20. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 21. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 22. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of cyclobenzaprine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 23. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dasatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 24. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of degarelix by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 25. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of desipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 26. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain conditions, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation, may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death. 27. Didanosine affects rilpivirine metabolism via hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Use caution and monitor patients closely. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution. Administer didanosine at least 2 hours before or several hours after rilpivirine. No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine. Didanosine should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal. 28. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of disopyramide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 29. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 47. Fingolimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 48. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of flecainide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 49. Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 50. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of fluconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 51. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of fluoxetine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 52. Fosamprenavir increases the effects of rilpivirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 53. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of foscarnet by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 54. Rilpivirine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 55. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 56. Gepirone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 57. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 59. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of haloperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 60. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Combination of rilpivirine and H2-receptor antagonists should be used cautiously, as co-administration may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 62. Ibutilide increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval.
